title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Incorporation of Proposals) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would incorporate tariff concession amendments into customs legislation, covering batch repairs, industrial processing, representative samples and terminology used in specified goods descriptions.
It would expressly cover batch repairs and remove industrial processing from one concession, directing those processing imports towards the separate Tradex Goods Scheme.
The amendments would apply retrospectively from 1 March 2013 and cover certain earlier imports where the time for calculating their duty had not yet arrived.
changes: References to value and amount would be removed from the representative samples concession.
By-laws could define the nature of samples eligible for the concession.
The vessel parts and materials concession would use gross construction tons as the measurement term.
Goods imported into warehouses before commencement could be covered if entered for home consumption after commencement.
summary.affected: Importers of goods covered by the amended repair, processing, sample and manufacturing-input concessions are affected.

speeches.speaker: Jason Clare
speeches.brief: Moved a bill making minor technical corrections to five items in schedule 4 of the Customs Tariff Act, including clarifying that a batch repair concession applies, removing outdated wording on industrial processing, and fixing a drafting error that had changed gross construction tons to tonnes for vessel parts duty concessions.

speeches.speaker: Michael Keenan
speeches.brief: Explained the Customs Tariff Amendment Bill makes minor technical corrections to five items in schedule 4 of the Customs Tariff Act, including reinstating the word wheelchairs and fixing a tons-to-tonnes error, implementing a tariff proposal that took effect on 1 March 2013.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Summed up the Customs Tariff Amendment Bill as formally incorporating five minor amendments to schedule 4 concessional duty items, tabled in February 2013, into the Customs Tariff Act following the 2012 Better Regulation Ministerial Partnership review.

speeches.speaker: Gary Humphries
speeches.brief: The bill amends the Customs Tariff Act 1995 to incorporate technical changes from a March 2013 tariff proposal, including clearer definitions and corrections to items 20, 21, 27, 30, and 35 in schedule 4. The coalition supported the amendments as uncontroversial.
